OCR on frame_118.00.png, frame_125.00.png, and frame_130.00.png (avg detection confidence 0.9600) reads: “p = w + 0.8s,” “w + s ≤ 60,” and “Work between 10 and 40 hours weekly,” with variable definitions for w, s, and p. So the visible optimization problem is to maximize productive hours p subject to w + s ≤ 60 and 10 ≤ w ≤ 40.

Using the OCR-grounded formula p = w + 0.8s and the listed options: A gives 15 + 0.8·45 = 51, B gives 20 + 0.8·40 = 52, C gives 12 + 0.8·48 = 50.4, and D gives 10 + 0.8·50 = 50. All four satisfy the OCR-visible constraints because each has w + s = 60 and work hours between 10 and 40.

Because every option uses the full 60 hours, maximizing p = w + 0.8s favors more work and less study; among the choices, B has the largest productive-hours total at 52. chart_analyzer on the same frames reports only text/equation constraints and explicitly says those frames do not show a plotted feasible region or highlighted maximizing point, so the decision comes from the OCR-grounded formula and option comparison rather than from a visible graph optimum.
Therefore the most productive listed weekly schedule is B: Work 20 hours, Study 40 hours.
